libSEDML maps the id of every KiSAO term (about 520 of them) to its name, so that it can name an algorithm or an algorithm parameter after its KiSAO term when it has no name. It used to do this using a global `std::map`, which meant building that map (and its strings) whenever libSEDML was loaded, and having the code that builds it in libOpenCOR. So, we build libSEDML with the patches in `patches`, which are applied by `cmake/applypatches.cmake` (to a freshly extracted copy of libSEDML's source code whenever they change):

- `libsedml-kisao-table.patch` replaces that `std::map` with a constant array, sorted by KiSAO id, in which we look up a KiSAO term using a binary search (`src/sedml/kisaomap.cpp`, `src/sedml/SedAlgorithm.cpp`, and `src/sedml/SedAlgorithmParameter.cpp`). This doesn't change libSEDML's behaviour.
